- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly, especially after sharp drops.
- After a large spike in price (true outcome > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward after 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model may lag; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% on the 3rd–5th day of sentiment reversal.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >85 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 1–3% per day until price stabilizes.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00–0.33) for 5+ days, model often underperforms; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for latent volatility.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward trend after forecast peak, model often fails to anticipate; reduce forecast by 2–4% on day 2–4 post-peak.
